Theme 080 · Characters & mascots

Pocket Pet

Pulse is a virtual pet living in a teal egg-shaped keychain with a greenish LCD and three buttons. It gets restless when a metric gets sick — a pixel ‘!’, wide eyes — and waits for you to press A. Dashboards were pets you had to feed; Pulse feeds itself.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Egg device — teal glossy shell with keychain loop; the product as an object
  • LCD pet — Pulse: 1-bit pixel critter with sleep, alert and happy sprites
  • Status icons — ‘!’, Z’s and hearts borrowed from virtual-pet UI
  • LCD readout — segment-style mono numbers (CHECKOUT −18%, since 09:42)
  • A · B · C buttons — physical choice: A = Roll back, B = Acknowledge
  • Grey herd — a row of grey devices = the dashboards you had to babysit

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Stepped sprite swap — pet frames switch at 4 fps (every 0.25 s = 8th note at 120 BPM), exactly like the handheld; no tweening on the LCD
  • Hop & land — devices drop 60 px with a 0.1 s squash (scaleY 0.9) on each downbeat
  • Button press — A depresses 6 px in 0.06 s, LCD inverts for 1 frame, release on the next 8th

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Why: A virtual pet is the perfect inversion of the pain: dashboards are needy pets you must check; Pulse is the pet that checks itself and calls you only when it matters. The three-button choice makes the human decision tactile. Risk: Nostalgia can read as a toy and LCD text is low-contrast; keep the LCD big in the proof shot and use real numbers.

Adapt to your product: Put your product’s key state on a tiny LCD with one pixel character, map your primary and secondary actions to buttons A and B, and use the grey device row for the tools you replace.

References: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamagotchi (egg-shaped handheld, 3 buttons, LCD icons that signal the pet’s needs)
